feature: Ask's component sheet: states you can see at a glance, a selection that moves, even margins
summary: On a sheet Ask makes, a coloured button's Hover is now a clearly darker shade than Default, and Pressed a clear step darker again. A segmented control or tab bar shows its selection on the segment each state names. A slider keeps its thumb in every look, and the page keeps a 64 to 96 point margin even when the model asks for 240.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no switch changed from its default, a blank picture 1440 by 1024, the built-in Qwen3.8 27B model.

try.do: File > New > Image, then press Ask (Command K).
Type: create a table of apple like quality base components that show different states and text, and press Send.
Wait for it (four to six minutes on this Mac).
Look across the Button row: Default, Hover and Pressed each a plainly different blue.
Compare with the build before: Hover nearly Default's blue, and the page 240 in from both edges.
Look at the Segmented Control row: the white selection sits on One, Two, Three in turn.
See it in the editor window.
try.shotNote: Photographed with the window behind another app, the way a walk leaves it. Blue buttons and picked controls show their background look here; with the window in front they take the accent colour.

try.do: Press Command Z once: the whole sheet goes.

evaluate: Does Hover now read as its own state, between Default and Pressed?
Is Pressed dark enough, or now too dark for a system blue?
Does each segmented state show its selection where you expect?
Do the margins feel even on both sides of the page?
rough: Not at the bar: Ask scored 84 and 74.8 on this build with the same request (judges 8, 8, 7, 7, 7 and 7, 7, 7, 7, 8), against 84 and 70.6 on the build before. Typography reached 8 once; aligned, designed and asked stay at 7. The task stays open (asking-for-a-sheet-of-components-gives-a-clean-t).

Two judges of three still read Hover and Pressed as close, though each now steps a whole state (1.35 lightness contrast) past the one before. Covered by this task (asking-for-a-sheet-of-components-gives-a-clean-t).

Keeping each state in one column down the table, with gaps, was tried and taken out: all three judges called the gaps patchy (picture 2026-11-02-component-sheet-column-gaps-tried.png). Rows with fewer states still leave the right side empty under the four-state Button row, and judges name it. Covered by this task (asking-for-a-sheet-of-components-gives-a-clean-t).

Judges sometimes read 'states and text' as asking for a row of text styles, and call a segmented control's One, Two, Three selections rather than states. Covered by this task (asking-for-a-sheet-of-components-gives-a-clean-t).
A badge's number sits a little off the centre of its circle, named in two runs. Covered by this task (asking-for-a-sheet-of-components-gives-a-clean-t).
The name chips over each look still cover the headers in the window. That is the-name-chips-over-component-copies-stay-clear.
The skill was not measured again this pass. The hover and selection changes only touch Ask's own planning; the thumb fix applies to both.
No mock covers this surface; the bar is the user's own words and the eval.
